note: This pointer stands in for the 3.1 MiB discovery_sweep.json, which is bulk run data and is hosted in the public Quilt package rather than in git, matching the convention 009.02 established for sweep.json, 009.06 for ladder_sweep.json and 009.08 for locator_sweep.json. Only discovery_analysis.py needs it: run the fetch command above to place the real file at experiments/sfp_representation/009_discovery_artifacts/discovery_sweep.json before running 'discovery_analysis.py --check'. Every other discovery module's --check path is self-contained and needs nothing fetched. Regenerating it locally instead of fetching costs about 12197 s of GPU-free CPU time via 'discovery_sweep.py'.
purpose: all 672 discovery runs: 2 declared blocks (the primary message and its one diagnosed repair) x 2 arms (one_anchor and the capacity-matched zero_anchor control) x 21 structural folds x 8 seeds, each one_anchor cell additionally carrying the 009.09a section 2 dual-anchor test-time control, the section 6 all-pairs chart audit under both reconstruction forms, the exact AGL(2,2) equivalence search and the section 7.5 fresh-relabelling transport test

quilt_hash.note: The Quilt manifest hashes entries with its own chunked scheme, so this value is expected to differ from the plain-file 'sha256' above. It is not a mismatch. Use 'sha256' to verify a fetched file with shasum.

run_digests.note: Digests of the per-run rows with the non-replayable wall-clock keys stripped, exactly as discovery_sweep.py records them. Recomputing them from a fetched file is a cheaper integrity check than a full byte comparison of the whole artifact.
